title: Fourth-moment tail bound for $B$-reasonable variables
statement:
Let $X$ be a real random variable on a probability space $\Omega$ that is $B$-reasonable and whose fourth power $X^4$ is integrable, and suppose its second moment is strictly positive, $\E[X^2] > 0$. Then for every $t > 0$,
\[
\Pr\!\bigl[\, X^4 \ge t^4\,(\E[X^2])^2 \,\bigr] \le \frac{B}{t^4}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: second moment E[X^2] is strictly positive
replaced:
If $X$ is $B$-reasonable and not equivalent to $0$ (its second moment is positive), then for
every $t > 0$,
\[
\Pr\bigl[\,|X| \ge t\,\norm{X}_2\,\bigr] \le \frac{B}{t^4}.
\]
